{"id":"JMAP-ic0j.26","title":"default-impl philosophy: spec-mandated extension methods silently no-op without override","description":"src/backend.rs — CalendarsBackend has six default-implemented extension methods
whose default behavior is "silently no-op the spec semantic":

  - parse_calendar_event_blobs (lines 447-462): default returns every blob
    in not_parsable. draft-ietf-jmap-calendars-26 §5.13 says the server
    parses iCalendar data; a backend that compiles+runs against the default
    silently violates §5.13 for every request.
  - get_availability (lines 471-484): default returns Ok(vec![]). draft §2.2
    is the entire Principal/getAvailability semantic; default backend returns
    "this principal is free at all times".
  - set_default_calendar (lines 414-421) and set_default_participant_identity
    (lines 432-439): defaults return empty SetDefaultResult. draft §3.3 and
    §4.3 onSuccessSetIsDefault always becomes a silent no-op.
  - compute_utc_times (lines 284-293): default returns (None, None). draft
    §5.2 utcStart/utcEnd are always absent.
  - get_calendar_events (lines 322-342): default delegates to get_objects,
    silently ignoring all §5.7 extras (recurrenceOverridesBefore/After,
    reduceParticipants, timeZone).
  - query_calendar_events (lines 368-389): default delegates to query_objects,
    silently ignoring expandRecurrences and timeZone (§5.11).

The canonical mail-server makes the equivalent spec-driven methods MANDATORY
(no defaults): MailBackend::import_email, find_thread_by_message_ids,
blob_exists, parse_email, copy_email, search_snippets all have no default
impl. The doc on blob_exists at crate-jmap-mail-server/src/backend.rs:194-198
explicitly justifies the policy:

    "There is no default implementation: requiring an explicit implementation
     forces each backend author to confront this distinction."

What goes wrong for the caller: a calendars backend author can implement
CalendarsBackend with zero overrides on the six methods above. The crate
compiles, the tests pass against MemoryBackend (which inherits the same
defaults). But every Principal/getAvailability returns "principal is always
free", every CalendarEvent/parse returns notParsable, every §4.3
onSuccessSetIsDefault is a no-op, every §5.7 timeZone is ignored, every §5.11
expandRecurrences is ignored. The wire protocol says success; the data is
silently wrong.

The convergence question is which way the canonical-template propagation
should go. Two coherent positions:

  (a) Calendars is wrong — drop the defaults, force every backend author
      to confront each spec method (mirror mail-server).
  (b) Mail is wrong — add defaults that silently no-op, accepting that
      backend authors have to read the spec to know what they're skipping.

Per workspace AGENTS.md "Canonical Templates", (a) is the default position
(propagate canonical→sibling). But the documented MemoryBackend deliberately
inherits these defaults, which suggests calendars maintainer intended (b).
Filed for explicit maintainer decision.

If (a) wins: remove the six default impls, propagate the mandatory-method
shape; the MemoryBackend explicit no-op overrides become the canonical
"we don't support this" pattern. If (b) wins: file the inverse propagation
into mail-server.","status":"open","priority":1,"issue_type":"task","owner":"mark@reviewcommit.com","created_at":"2026-05-15T17:11:42Z","created_by":"Mark Atwood","updated_at":"2026-05-15T17:11:42Z","metadata":{},"dependencies":[{"issue_id":"","depends_on_id":"","type":"parent-child","created_at":"2026-05-15T10:11:42Z","created_by":"Mark Atwood","metadata":"{}"}]}

{"notes":"DECISION NEEDED (triage 2026-10-19 at 9fdbbbcf): Question for Mark: across the workspace, should a backend-trait method that carries a spec-mandated semantic (not a permission/policy hook, which JMAP-bghk keeps fail-open) have a default implementation that does nothing?

Option A (mail-server canonical, strict): remove all six calendars defaults. Every backend, including MemoryBackend and the test mocks, then writes an explicit override that says "not supported". Most consistent with the AGENTS.md Canonical Templates rule. It breaks every downstream CalendarsBackend implementor seven times over.

Option B (hybrid, the 2026-05-15 comment): remove the defaults only where the no-op puts wrong data on the wire:
- parse_calendar_event_blobs (every blob reported as notParsable)
- get_availability (principal always free)
- set_default_calendar and set_default_participant_identity (isDefault silently dropped)

Keep the defaults for compute_utc_times and get/query_calendar_events, where the result is data that is missing or ignored rather than wrong, and change their rustdoc to a "MUST override for real semantics" line. Breaking, but only four methods.

Option C (calendars canonical): keep the defaults and accept silent no-ops; file the reverse propagation into mail-server. Not recommended, because it spreads the silent-failure footgun.

Recommendation: Option B. One nuance: the two set_default methods may arguably keep their defaults. §3.3/§4.3 already say a failed onSuccessSetIsDefault returns no error to the client, so a backend with no per-account default is spec-legal. That would leave only get_availability and parse_calendar_event_blobs mandatory.

Once ratified:
1. Delete the chosen default bodies in calendars-server/src/backend.rs.
2. Add explicit overrides to MemoryBackend and each test backend in lib.rs, event.rs and principal.rs. The existing memory.rs set_default overrides stay.
3. Rename principal.rs:169 so it tests MemoryBackend's explicit override, not a trait default.
4. Record the policy with `bd remember` and add it to AGENTS.md.
5. Apply the same rule to JMAP-ops7.23 (drop the default) and JMAP-ops7.24 (pick a single pattern).

Cost is about 100-200 lines, mostly boilerplate overrides in test backends."}
